quick: Test 10,000 KIU IV, then loading 1-2 million KIU + 1-2 million KIU in pump prime, then 250,000-500,000 KIU/h (max ~7 million KIU/course)
IV use only; not related to meals
Use only if benefit justifies risk
Not orally bioavailable - no systemic effect on infant expected
No dose adjustment; can trigger renal dysfunction - caution if pre-existing
Anaphylaxis, renal function, ACT (celite >=750 s / kaolin >=480 s)
summary: Aprotinin (Trasylol) is a broad-spectrum serine protease inhibitor with antifibrinolytic action, indicated in the EU - under restricted, controlled conditions - for prophylactic use to reduce blood loss and transfusion in adults at high risk of major blood loss undergoing ISOLATED coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery (not combined with other cardiovascular surgery). It inhibits plasmin, kallikrein and trypsin, forming reversible enzyme-inhibitor complexes. Dosing is in kallikrein inhibitor units (KIU): a 10,000 KIU test dose, a 1-2 million KIU loading dose, a further 1-2 million KIU in the pump prime, then a 250,000-500,000 KIU/h infusion, generally not exceeding 7 million KIU per course. The chief hazard is anaphylaxis (especially on re-exposure within 12 months) and renal dysfunction/thrombotic events; it was suspended in 2007-2008 after the BART trial mortality concern and later reinstated for the restricted CABG indication. It is not a heparin-sparing agent.
indications: Prophylactic use to reduce blood loss and blood transfusion in adult patients at high risk of major blood loss undergoing isolated cardiopulmonary bypass graft surgery (CABG not combined with other cardiovascular surgery)

dosage.d: 10,000 KIU (1 mL) IV at least 10 minutes before the remainder of the dose; an H1- and H2-antagonist may be given 15 minutes beforehand
dosage.n: Give only with anaphylaxis treatment immediately available; patient supine

dosage.d: 1-2 million KIU by slow IV injection or infusion over 20-30 minutes
dosage.n: Maximum infusion rate 5-10 mL/min via central line

dosage.d: A further 1-2 million KIU added to the cardiopulmonary bypass pump prime
dosage.n: Add aprotinin and heparin during recirculation of the prime to ensure dilution before admixture (physical incompatibility)
Total per course generally not to exceed 7 million KIU

admin: Intravenous use only; administer with the patient supine via a central venous catheter, not sharing the lumen with other drugs
Always give the 10,000 KIU test dose at least 10 minutes before the main dose, with anaphylaxis treatment ready on-site
Maintain full heparin anticoagulation - aprotinin is NOT a heparin-sparing agent
Consider an aprotinin-specific IgG antibody test before dosing; do not use if positive
Inspect for particulate matter/discoloration; discard unused solution
moa: Aprotinin forms reversible stoichiometric enzyme-inhibitor complexes that inhibit human trypsin, plasmin, plasma kallikrein and tissue kallikrein, thereby inhibiting fibrinolysis. It also inhibits contact-phase activation of coagulation, which both initiates coagulation and promotes fibrinolysis, reducing perioperative blood loss.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to aprotinin or any excipient
Positive aprotinin-specific IgG antibody test (high anaphylaxis risk)
Suspected previous exposure to aprotinin (including aprotinin-containing fibrin sealants) within the last 12 months if no IgG antibody test is available
relative: CABG combined with other cardiovascular surgery (outside the restricted indication)
Pre-existing renal impairment or renal risk factors (e.g. concomitant aminoglycosides)
monitor: Signs of allergic/anaphylactic reaction during and after administration
Activated clotting time (celite ACT >=750 s or kaolin ACT >=480 s)

preg: No adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women; animal studies showed no teratogenic or embryotoxic effects. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; severe adverse reactions (anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest) and their treatment can themselves harm the fetus. Placental permeation appears very slow.
lact: It is unknown whether aprotinin is excreted in human milk, but it is not bioavailable after oral administration, so any drug present in milk is not expected to have a systemic effect on the breastfed child.
renal: No special dose adjustment is required for decreased renal function. However, aprotinin can trigger renal dysfunction, especially with pre-existing renal impairment - perform a careful risk/benefit assessment and monitor serum creatinine. No pharmacokinetic data in terminal renal insufficiency.
hepatic: No data are available on dosage recommendations in patients with hepatic dysfunction.

major: Thrombolytic/fibrinolytic agents (streptokinase, urokinase, alteplase) - aprotinin has a dose-dependent inhibitory effect, antagonizing thrombolysis
moderate: Aminoglycosides - additive risk factor for aprotinin-associated renal dysfunction
Heparin - aprotinin prolongs celite ACT and PTT but is NOT heparin-sparing; do not use PTT/APTT to guide heparin dosing during use
minor: ACE inhibitors (captopril/enalapril) - pharmacology literature suggests aprotinin may blunt the hypotensive effect via kallikrein-kinin inhibition (not in the official SmPC interaction section)
interactions.diagnostics: Markedly prolongs celite activated clotting time (use kaolin ACT, fixed heparin dosing, or protamine titration instead of PTT/APTT to monitor heparin); may raise serum creatinine.

common: Hypersensitivity-related symptoms on infusion (flushing, pruritus, rash)
serious: Anaphylactic / anaphylactoid reactions (higher on re-exposure - up to ~5% within 6 months)
Myocardial ischaemia, coronary occlusion/thrombosis, myocardial infarction (most serious reported ADR)
Arterial and venous thrombosis (renal, pulmonary, cerebral)
Acute renal failure, renal tubular necrosis, oliguria
emergency: Anaphylactic shock (potentially life-threatening, especially on re-exposure)
Acute myocardial infarction or major thrombotic event

monitoring: Continuous observation for allergic/anaphylactic reaction (stop infusion immediately if it occurs)
Renal function (serum creatinine), particularly with pre-existing impairment or aminoglycosides
Activated clotting time using celite (>=750 s) or kaolin (>=480 s); maintain full heparin anticoagulation
Aprotinin-specific IgG antibody test before dosing where possible
counsel: This medicine reduces blood loss during heart bypass surgery and is given only in carefully selected patients
Tell the team if you have ever received aprotinin (including in surgical glue/fibrin sealant) - it must not be re-used within 12 months without a special blood test
A small test dose is given first because of the risk of severe allergic reactions
You will be monitored closely for allergic reactions, kidney function and clotting during surgery
It does not replace your usual blood-thinning (heparin) during the operation
pk: Rapid distribution into extracellular space after IV injection
Achieved during/immediately after the slow IV loading infusion
Initial (distribution) half-life 0.3-0.7 h; terminal elimination half-life approximately 5-10 h
Maintained by continuous intra-operative infusion; metabolised to peptides/amino acids by renal lysosomal activity (<5% excreted as active drug)
Store per national SmPC (typically refrigerated/controlled temperature per product); do not freeze
pearls: RESTRICTED use - EU authorisation is only for isolated CABG (not combined cardiovascular surgery); aprotinin was suspended in 2007-2008 after the BART trial mortality concern and reinstated under controlled conditions
ALWAYS give the 10,000 KIU test dose first, supine, with anaphylaxis treatment ready
Do NOT use if exposed (including fibrin sealants) within the last 12 months unless a negative IgG antibody test is available - re-exposure anaphylaxis risk is highest in the first 6-12 months
It is NOT a heparin-sparing agent - maintain full heparin and monitor with ACT (celite >=750 s / kaolin >=480 s), not PTT/APTT
Avoid or use great caution with pre-existing renal impairment and concomitant aminoglycosides
missed: Not applicable - aprotinin is administered intra-operatively by the anaesthetic/surgical team on a defined schedule, not as repeated outpatient dosing.
overdose: There is no specific antidote and no specific substance to counteract its effects. Management is supportive, with attention to anaphylaxis, renal function and thrombotic complications.
